papers.abstract: Demand response aggregators require consumers' private flexibility information to dispatch loads efficiently. Yet self-interested consumers have incentives to misreport it. This paper investigates how much information heterogeneous consumers can credibly convey through nonbinding, unverifiable reports, and how a pre-announced retail tariff can improve this revelation. We model this interaction as a multi-sender strategic communication game with state-dependent bias, using the cheap-talk framework. The aggregator maximizes social welfare, and consumers have private valuations and quadratic payoffs. Closed-form conditions identify when the set of dispatched consumers is invariant to the reports. Under these conditions, reporting incentives decouple into independent single-sender subgames. We derive a closed-form uniform tariff that simultaneously minimizes the mean-squared strategic bias of all dispatched consumers. In this regime, the welfare loss relative to full communication is expressed as a weighted sum of residual posterior variances, showing that every equilibrium weakly improves expected social welfare over no communication. Numerical studies support the theoretical results and show that, when consumers coordinate on informative equilibria, strategic communication with the proposed bias-minimizing tariff recovers most of the full-communication welfare gain over no communication.
papers.title: Pricing for Information Revelation in Demand Response: A Strategic Communication Approach

papers.abstract: Hundreds of millions of people now ask large language model (LLM) chatbots for health advice, which raises a question that is simple to pose and hard to answer: does everyone get the same advice? We audit six widely deployed LLMs from four providers on smoking cessation, a domain with codified clini- cal guidance and substantial public-health stakes, by putting the same four cessation questions to twelve user personas that differ in life stage, self-described expertise, and smoking history, for a total of 2,880 responses. What the models say depends on who appears to be asking. Every model named FDA-approved prescription cessation medications less often to teen personas than to adult personas, by 32 to 67 percentage points, and in five of six models a persona presenting health- care expertise received fewer facts than a persona presenting none. We then evaluate one deployable intervention: a short system prompt specifying a factual floor, the set of core med- ical facts every user should receive when they are relevant, while leaving tone, vocabulary, and framing free to adapt. The prompt narrows persona differences in every model, but its effect on overall fact coverage varies in both magnitude and direction across models, so a prompt validated on one system cannot be assumed to transfer to another. Two cautions frame these results. Equal mention rates are not always the correct clinical target, because prescription cessation pharmacother- apy is not recommended for minors, so a defensible factual floor must be age-aware rather than uniform. And because our personas vary on several attributes at once, we report scenario- level differences rather than isolated effects of age or expertise. We release all 2,880 responses and the analysis code.
papers.title: Same Question, Different Answers: Auditing Persona-Dependent Variation in Six LLMs on Smoking-Cessation Advice

papers.abstract: We study the processes $e^+e^-\toΥ_J(1D)η$ and $e^+e^-\toΥ_J(1D)π^+π^-$ at center-of-mass energies $\sqrt{s}$=(10.73 -- 11.02) GeV using a $142.5\,\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ data sample, including 122~fb$^{-1}$ near the $Υ$(10860) peak ($\sqrt{s}$ = 10.866 GeV), collected with the Belle detector at the KEKB asymmetric-energy $e^+e^-$ collider. From the peak sample, the products of Born cross section times branching fraction are obtained for $σ_{\rm Born}(e^+e^-\toΥ_J(1D)η)$ or $σ_{\rm Born}(e^+e^-\toΥ_J(1D)π^+π^-)$ and ${\cal B}(Υ_J(1D)\toχ_{b1}γ)$ or ${\cal B}(Υ_J(1D)\toχ_{b2}γ)$ for each $Υ_J(1D)$ state. The corresponding branching fractions for $Υ(10860)$ decays are also obtained. The significances of the $Υ_1(1D)$, $Υ_2(1D)$, and $Υ_3(1D)$ signals are 4.8$σ$, ${>}10σ$, and 3.0$σ$, respectively, including systematic uncertainties. The mass for $Υ_2(1D)$ is measured to be $(10167.0\pm 1.0\pm 0.2)$ MeV/$c^2$, where the first and second uncertainties are statistical and systematic. The mass splittings $Δm_{12}=m(Υ_2(1D))-m(Υ_1(1D))$ and $Δm_{23}=m(Υ_3(1D))-m(Υ_2(1D))$ are $(11.8\pm1.5\pm0.4)$ MeV/$c^2$ and $(7.6\pm2.4\pm0.6)$ MeV/$c^2$, respectively.~We determine the energy dependence of the cross sections for $e^+e^-\toΥ_J(1D)η$ and $e^+e^-\toΥ_J(1D)π^+π^-$ for the $Υ_1(1D)$, $Υ_2(1D)$, and $Υ_3(1D)$ states, combined.
papers.title: First measurement of the masses of the $Υ_1(1D)$ and $Υ_3(1D)$ states and the energy dependence of the cross sections for $e^+e^-\toΥ_J(1D)η$ and $e^+e^-\toΥ_J(1D)π^+π^-$

papers.abstract: Machine learning continues to emerge as an important tool to be utilised within structural engineering and structural health monitoring, due to its ability to accurately and quickly perform both regression and classification tasks. However, a purely data driven approach has its limitations, particularly where we lack data from relevant environmental and operational conditions, a situation that has led to the development of physics-informed machine learners for structural health monitoring. These "grey-box" models take into account the physical insight that an engineer would have about the structure they are modelling and have shown promising results in the structural engineering field among many others. This work compares black and grey-box models through a "green" lens, comparing them in terms of their environmental impact, and investigating how the high extrapolative performance of grey-box models can reduce their runtimes and therefore carbon emissions. The authors aim to develop physics-informed models with reduced computational costs, while maintaining high performance, illustrated through a structural health monitoring case study.
papers.title: Green Physics-Informed Machine Learning Models For Structural Health Monitoring

papers.abstract: Directly determining graded materials from prescribed wave amplitude and phase is an inverse-design method developed following transformation optics (TO), which enables reflectionless propagation for an incidence wave. However, exiting formulations of this inverted method yields Hermitian media and are thus not applicable to non-Hermitian (NH) photonics. In this Letter, we extend this method to NH media, thereby offering more freedom for manipulating waves of no reflection. Our picture of curved-space powered with spatially distributed gain and loss, is exemplified by three types: amplitude control, phase conversion, and direction shunting. These examples showcase precise wave manipulation in a surprisingly simple manner, which is implementable in photonic platform using similar techniques employed in TO.
papers.title: Non-Hermitian curved space via inverted wave equation

papers.abstract: Bengali, spoken by over 230 million people, remains severely under-resourced in spoken language research. Existing open Bengali ASR corpora are confined to short, read or crowd-sourced speech and lack speaker diarization and long-form audio. We present Lipi-Ghor, a large-scale weakly-supervised Bengali speech corpus comprising 885 hours of audio sourced from 998 YouTube videos across 596 unique channels, spanning 17 diverse domains including audiobooks, drama, religious sermons, news, and regional dialects. Each recording is annotated in SSTT format (Speaker, Speech, Transcription, Timestamp), which combines automated diarization with Bengali YouTube caption tracks. To our knowledge, Lipi-Ghor is the first Bengali speech corpus to pair large-scale coverage with speaker-diarized, long-form audio annotations, both of which are absent from existing open Bengali resources. We also present the construction methodology as a replicable pipeline for any language with a sufficient captioned YouTube presence. Targeted channel curation across a handful of rich domains yields corpus scales that were previously out of reach for low-resource languages. We benchmark four widely-used ASR models under zero-shot and fine-tuned conditions. All four degrade consistently on emotive, dialectal, and long-form content. Because caption targets are noisy, we also release a human-annotated gold evaluation split, verified by 17 volunteer annotators over 30 hours of human-in-the-loop correction and stratified across all 17 domains. We release our original contributions (video-ID lists, diarization output, pipeline code, and the gold annotations) under CC-BY-4.0, and distribute caption-derived transcripts for research use only; no raw audio is redistributed.
papers.title: Lipi-Ghor: A Large-Scale, Diarized, Multi-Domain Bengali Speech Corpus and a Scalable Pipeline for Building It

papers.abstract: Between the digital and quantum paradigms lies the emerging field of quantum-inspired analog computing, in which classical waves emulate quantum circuits. We introduce wavebits -- classical wave analogs of qubits whose amplitudes are carried by physical oscillatory signals -- and show that any nonseparable N-qubit state can be encoded in 2N narrowband signals that remain locally separable at every instant; the nonseparable correlations are recovered at readout by time-averaged demodulation over auxiliary carrier frequencies, the nonseparability channels. We prove that any two-qubit gate unravels into the time-averaged tensor product of two local time-varying operators, and that arbitrary circuits are emulated with a base-frequency count scaling linearly in the number of entangling two-qubit gates, independent of qubit number for a fixed gate count. The exponential cost of the 2^N-dimensional state reappears at readout and in the averaging time of circuits with many two-qubit gates, not in circuit execution, as quantified by an analytic error bound that doubles as a hardware design rule. A mixed-signal prototype emulates Bell state generation, controlled-NOT gates, phase kickback, and Bloch-sphere rotations at fidelities above 0.99, and numerical benchmarks against exact statevectors validate the scheme for up to six qubits. The architecture is directly implementable in acoustic, photonic, and mixed-signal platforms.
papers.title: Classical Analog Emulation of Quantum Circuits via Time-Averaged Dynamic States

papers.abstract: The conditions governing the existence and evolution of trapped sausage waves in photospheric magnetic pores are investigated, with particular emphasis on the limitations of analytical cut-off criteria and the role of viscous dissipation. A pore is modelled as a cylindrical magnetic flux tube with smoothly varying radial profiles of magnetic field and density, subject to the constraint that its temperature is lower than that of the surrounding atmosphere. For finite plasma-$β$, the linearised equations governing sausage-mode perturbations are derived, and an initial-value problem is solved numerically to obtain the full spatio-temporal evolution of the waves. The applicability of the analytical cut-off relation derived for a flux tube with step-function equilibrium profiles is examined, revealing that its predictions depend on the equilibrium parameters. The simulations reveal distinct wave behaviours across different parameter regimes, including the simultaneous excitation of trapped fast and slow sausage waves for a representative photospheric parameter set. Viscous damping is further investigated through the temporal evolution of the wave energy. Energy dissipation increases with decreasing viscous Reynolds number, increasing longitudinal wavenumber, and increasing radial magnetic-field contrast. These trends are consistent with enhanced viscous damping associated with increasingly fine spatial gradients generated through phase mixing. The findings highlight the importance of radial equilibrium structure in assessing sausage-wave trapping and demonstrate the sensitivity of wave-energy dissipation to the physical parameters of photospheric magnetic pores.
papers.title: Trapped sausage modes in magnetic pores: existence criteria and viscous damping

papers.abstract: Regular black holes (RBHs) can be seen as possible alternatives to standard black holes (BHs), since these geometries do not have a curvature singularity. As a way of improving our knowledge of such geometries, we can investigate how the astrophysical environment interacts with RBHs and compare the results with those obtained in the framework of standard BHs. In this work, we aim to study the absorption and scattering cross sections of massive scalar waves impinging on Ayón-Beato-García and Bardeen charged RBH geometries, focusing on understanding the role played by the field's mass. Concerning the absorption spectrum, our numerical results show that the total absorption cross section decreases as we increase the field's mass for fixed values of the BH charge. In turn, in the scattering spectrum, an increase in the mass of the field leads to wider interference widths for field velocities larger than a critical value, $v_c$. Moreover, we also compare our numerical results with the classical and semiclassical approximations, showing that they agree very well within the appropriate limits. We also draw comparisons with the results of the Reissner-Nordström metric. In particular, we show that the mass of the field contributes to finding situations in which the absorption and scattering spectra of regular and standard BHs are similar for arbitrary values of the field frequency and scattering angle, considering low- to near-extreme BH charges.
papers.title: Absorption and scattering spectra of massive scalar waves in charged regular black hole spacetimes

papers.abstract: This work introduces a method to equip data-driven polynomial chaos expansion surrogate models with intervals that quantify the predictive uncertainty of the surrogate. To that end, jackknife-based conformal prediction is integrated into regression-based polynomial chaos expansions. The jackknife algorithm uses leave-one-out residuals to generate predictive intervals around the predictions of the polynomial chaos surrogate. The jackknife+ extension additionally requires leave-one-out model predictions. Both methods allow to use the entire dataset for model training and do not require a hold-out dataset for prediction interval calibration. The key to efficient implementation is to leverage the linearity of the polynomial chaos regression model, so that leave-one-out residuals and, if necessary, leave-one-out model predictions can be computed with analytical, closed-form expressions. This eliminates the need for repeated model re-training. The conformalized polynomial chaos expansion method is first validated on four benchmark models and then applied to two electrical engineering design use-cases. The method produces predictive intervals that provide the target coverages, even for low-accuracy models trained with small datasets. At the same time, training data availability plays a crucial role in improving the empirical coverage and narrowing the predictive interval, as well as in reducing their variability over different training datasets.
papers.title: Conformalized Polynomial Chaos Expansion for Uncertainty-aware Surrogate Modeling

papers.abstract: We study the supernova (SN) shock breakout (SBO) from an optically thick stellar wind. The SN ejecta-wind interaction forms a forward shock (FS) plus reverse shock (RS) structure. The RS's internal energy and shock velocity are both a fraction $μ\lesssim1/6$ of the FS's. The lower RS velocity makes it easier to build up local thermal equilibrium (LTE) and generate blackbody (BB) emission. In the same time a $μ^{-1}\gtrsim6$ times larger non-BB emission may be produced by the likely non-LTE FS. We apply the theory to analyze the recent detected type Ic-BL SN2026gzf associated X-ray flash EP260321a, and find it is naturally accounted for by a SN wind breakout: the $\sim0.13$\,keV, thermal SBO emission can be produced by the RS during the interaction of a typical type Ic-BL SN ejecta ($E_k\sim10^{52}$erg and $M_e\sim1M_\odot$) and a stellar wind with a mass $M_w\sim10^{-4}M_\odot$ confined within a radius $r_w\sim10^{13}$cm; the X-ray rise time is mainly determined by the RS emission time, whereas the long duration and decrease time are due to the scatterings of SBO photons by a distant shell-like medium which has a large photosphere, $r_{ph}\sim10^{14}$\,cm; the early, within 30\,ks, optical emission can be naturally explained by the cooling emission of a shocked pure C/O envelope, since the observed SBO onset is delayed by $\gtrsim$ a few ks due to the large medium photosphere. BB+non-BB components from RS and FS, respectively, may be common in SN wind breakouts. SBO observations can be crucial in the study of progenitor stars by providing information for the ejecta from the SN explosion and the nearby wind from the pre-SN activities.
papers.title: Double-Shock Radiation in Supernova Wind Breakout and EP260321a

papers.abstract: We present a Bayesian framework, Two-stage Inference for Light curve DEcomposition (TILDE), for mapping the accretion disk and the broad line region (BLR) from active galactic nuclei (AGN) multi-band light curves. By inferring delayed BLR contamination from the underlying disk variability, TILDE provides the delay measurements of the disk as well as the BLR. We validate TILDE using synthetic data, finding that TILDE recovers the known time delays of the disk and BLR. By applying TILDE to the Seoul National University AGN Monitoring Project sample, we find that the inferred BLR light curves match the observed H$β$ emission light curves, providing consistent BLR lags compared to the reported H$β$ lags. Using the lag spectrum, effectively corrected for the BLR contamination, we find that the disk size is broadly consistent with the standard thin-disk model, suggesting that BLR contamination can significantly bias the disk size derived from the cross-correlation analysis of the broad-band photometry. These results demonstrate that the new inference method is a powerful tool for determining both disk and BLR sizes from broad-band photometry in the era of time-domain surveys.
papers.title: Unveiling Accretion-Disk Reverberation Beneath BLR Contamination with TILDE

papers.abstract: We investigate the observational differences between the Ellis--Bronnikov (EB) wormhole and the Schwarzschild black hole (BH) by performing general relativistic radiative transfer (GRRT) simulations. We consider a spherically symmetric steady-state accretion flow and perform GRRT simulations incorporating synchrotron emission. For both the EB wormhole and the Schwarzschild BH, the simulated images consist of a central shadow region and a bright photon ring. We find that both the shadow region and the photon ring of the EB wormhole are brighter than those of the Schwarzschild BH. These differences arise from the absence of an event horizon in the EB wormhole, allowing the emission from the accreting matter around and beyond the throat to contribute to the intensity. We also compare the simulated images with the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) observations of M87*. Although the total flux and the ring diameter are comparable with the EHT results, our models with the spherically symmetric accretion flow cannot reproduce the deep central brightness depression observed by the EHT, for both the EB wormhole and the Schwarzschild BH. This indicates that a non-spherical accretion flow is required for a detailed comparison with the EHT image.
papers.title: Ellis-Bronnikov Wormhole Shadows with Spherically Symmetric Accretion Flow

papers.abstract: Modern serving systems for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models adopt hybrid data-expert parallelism: expert parallelism (EP) shards experts across GPUs to scale capacity, while data parallelism (DP) replicates attention layers across instances to process independent requests. Existing systems bind each request's attention, MoE communication, and KV cache to a single instance. Because attention latency scales with KV cache size while MoE communication latency scales with batch size, this binding cannot balance both simultaneously, producing EP stragglers; it also fragments KV memory across instances, inflating tail latency under long contexts. While existing context parallelism (CP) mitigates these constraints, existing group-level and uniform CP designs incur prohibitive communication and attention-side overheads. We present NanoCP, which decouples MoE communication from KV cache placement and achieves dual balance through dynamic context parallelism (DCP). DCP assigns each request a context-parallel degree sized to its KV footprint: long requests distribute attention across multiple instances; short requests remain local. This dynamic parallelism effectively liquefies the KV cache across DP instances within each node, balancing both the per-instance KV cache occupancy and batch sizes without unnecessary load-balancing costs. To bridge DCP with static execution, NanoCP introduces an ahead-of-time (AOT) graph engine paired with a custom routing-based communication backend. Experimental results show that, under 99% TPOT-SLO attainment, NanoCP achieves $3.27\times$ and $2.11\times$ the maximum sustainable request rate of the best-performing vLLM baseline on the DeepSeek-V3 Issue 1% and Issue 5% workloads, respectively, while reducing P99 TPOT by $1.94\times$ and $2.01\times$ on the same two workloads, respectively.
papers.title: NanoCP: Taming Load Imbalance in Data-Expert Parallel Decoding under Variable-Length Workloads

papers.abstract: Strong light-matter coupling in optical waveguides provides a versatile platform for engineering hybrid polaritonic modes and their dispersion. Here we investigate multimode exciton-photon coupling in visible semiconductor waveguides supporting several transverse electric modes. Using rigorous coupled-wave analysis combined with a coupled-oscillator model, we show that the photonic band structure can be engineered across a range of regimes, from conventional multimode strong coupling to the superstrong coupling regime, where the Rabi splitting becomes comparable to the spacing between adjacent photonic modes. In the latter regime, hybridization between orthogonal electromagnetic modes is enabled by restricting the active material to a subregion of the mode volume where the photonic modes exhibit strong mutual overlap. This breaking of the orthogonality leads to polaritonic branches whose composition can be tuned among several photonic modes and the exciton. We demonstrate that small shifts of the exciton resonance produce pronounced changes in the propagation constants of different polariton branches, enabling exciton-controlled phase modulation through modal interference and, in the superstrong coupling regime, direct modal switching across a continuous S-shaped dispersion. The resulting figures of merit predict $π$ phase shifts for exciton energy shifts of only a few meV over propagation lengths of tens of micrometers, while larger shifts are still required for mode switching. These results establish multimode waveguide polaritons as a versatile platform spanning multiple coupling regimes, for compact phase and intensity control in integrated photonic architectures.
papers.title: Exciton-Tunable Phase Control and Superstrong Coupling Through Multimode Polariton Engineering in Planar Waveguides

papers.abstract: With a 35-day orbital period and $\sim$0.5 eccentricity, TOI-2257 b occupies a sparsely populated corner of transiting mini-Neptune parameter space and may lie near the orbital distance at which tidal and atmospheric escape process become negligible. To test this hypothesis, we performed simulations of the combined stellar, tidal, and atmospheric evolution and confirmed that TOI-2257 b does lie near this boundary, regardless of whether it formed with or without a primordial hydrogen envelope. In the mini-Neptune scenario, we find that all cases retain an envelope of at least 0.02 M$_\oplus$ for 8 Gyr, but that the envelope mass can be halved if it was initially larger than 0.2 M$_\oplus$. We find that tidal evolution only occurs for cases with initial envelope masses larger than 0.02 M$_\oplus$ because their radii are large enough to generate significant torques. In the super-Earth scenario, the planet could lose $\sim$10 Earth ocean masses of surface water during the $\sim$75 Myr pre-main sequence and therefore could be habitable if it formed with $\gtrsim$2x Earth's surface water mass. The predicted tidal heating surface flux tends to be similar to Io, with no cases approaching the flux required to drive a runaway greenhouse. We find that if the planet is rocky, then eccentricities larger than 0.62 today are strongly disfavored, implying that larger eccentricities could confirm the gaseous nature of the planet. These results suggest that TOI-2257 b could provide valuable constraints on mini-Neptune properties and new insight into the radius valley shape as a function of eccentricity.
papers.title: The Limits of Tidal Circularization and Atmospheric Escape for Mini-Neptunes and Super-Earths: The Case of TOI-2257 b

papers.abstract: Planet formation requires growth over 12 orders of magnitude in size, from micron-sized dust grains to fully formed planets. The formation of km sized planetesimals is the most challenging stage, where radial drift and fragmentation rapidly remove meter- sized solids from the protoplanetary disc. Overcoming this barrier requires favourable conditions for streaming instability to concentrate solids. These problems are exacerbated in binary star systems, where gravitational perturbations and disc truncation reduce the efficiency of planetesimal formation pathways. Planetesimal capture provides an alternative mechanism where unbound planetesimals are captured by the protoplanetary disc through gas-drag, potentially bypassing the most restrictive growth stages. We investigate this process in circumstellar and circumbinary discs using over 30 million numerical experiments across a range of binary separations. For circumstellar discs, capture of large planetesimals is suppressed below 50 au, with the strongest reduction at around 10 au, broadly consistent with the observed decrease in planet occurrence in binaries. Tight binaries can still capture O(1) km-sized planetesimals, increasing to O(10) km-sized in wider systems during the birth cluster's lifetime. Circumbinary discs are much less efficient, with capture rates dropping to around 1 percent of the single-star case for binaries above 1 au and becoming negligible for large planetesimals at wider separations. Overall, planetesimal capture provides a supplementary channel for delivering solids to binary systems and mitigating inefficiencies in in-situ planetesimal formation.
papers.title: Capture of Interstellar Planetesimals in Protoplanetary Discs in Binary Star Systems

papers.abstract: Major open-source serving stacks reuse the key-value tensors of a shared prefix by default. We measure what this prefix reuse costs in reproducibility. Holding model, decoding, seed and request order fixed at batch size one, we ran an eighty-episode multi-turn agentic tool-use workload with prefix reuse on and off across two engines and four weight formats. Without prefix reuse, repeated runs reproduced every token and log-probability in all ten configurations. With it, cache-hit and recompute paths diverged on both engines. On llama.cpp with GGUF weights this path divergence rises with quantization: for Qwen2.5-7B over ten independent server histories, it reached 37.4 percent of episodes at 16-bit and 82.5 percent at four-bit. Near-tie decisions became only about 1.2 times as common, while the cache-path change in top-two margins grew 4.9-fold from 16-bit to three-bit. Serving four-bit weights through 16-bit kernels left divergence not detectably different from 16-bit, placing the amplification mainly in the quantized execution path. At Q4_K_M, run-to-run divergence came mainly from llama.cpp's server-level prompt cache: under the canonical episode order it moved divergence by 37.5 points, and at its default, divergence spanned 20.0 to 28.7 percent under five random orders. With cache state restored, each path reproduced exactly while the two still differed. In the tested stacks, cached serving is irreproducible because the cache state is absent from the request and not reset by default. A single-turn bridge shows path divergence reaching task outcomes with no detectable net change in accuracy. We release the harness, logs, and analysis pipeline.
papers.title: Same Request, Different Answer: Quantization Amplifies Cache-Induced Divergence in LLM Serving

papers.abstract: We report redshifted cool gas toward the central star-forming region of the nearby starburst dwarf galaxy NGC 4214. HST/COS spectra show low-ionization absorbers redshifted relative to the systemic velocity, most clearly in SII ($Δv=19.8\pm2.6\ {\rm km\,s^{-1}}$) and supported by MgII ($Δv=30.3\pm3.0\ {\rm km\,s^{-1}}$), while PII remains tentative ($Δv=7.5\pm3.4\ {\rm km\,s^{-1}}$). The Keck/HIRES spectra also reveal a redshifted CaII absorption component ($Δv=25.6\pm1.5\ {\rm km\,s^{-1}}$). Because the absorption is detected against the central UV or optical continuum, the gas must lie in the foreground of the star-forming region and is moving away from the observer and toward the background UV source in projection. A VLA--THINGS HI spectrum extracted at the COS position within one VLA beam also shows a redshifted neutral component at $v_{\rm hel}=329.2\pm0.9\ {\rm km\ s^{-1}}$, offset by $38.2\pm1.3\ {\rm km\ s^{-1}}$ from systemic and by $27.6\pm1.0\ {\rm km\ s^{-1}}$ from the dominant local HI component. The FAST HI mapping further reveals an extended, kinematically disturbed neutral disk, with residual structures relative to a warped-disk model. Together, the redshifted UV absorption, the redshifted HI component, and the disturbed large-scale HI velocity field show that the central anomalous cool gas is observed in a galaxy with a disturbed extended neutral disk. This geometry suggests that the redshifted cool gas may trace inflow or recycled fallback toward the central region, although warped-disk or non-circular disk motions cannot be fully excluded.
papers.title: Redshifted Cool Gas in the Disturbed HI Disk of the Starburst Dwarf NGC 4214

papers.abstract: There are conflicting predictions and reports on the character of the exciton Mott transition (EMT) in monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides. It could be either a discontinuous or a continuous transition from the excitonic to the plasma phase, with important implications for devices such as photoswitches. To resolve the nature of the transition in monolayer WS$_2$, we study its ultrafast optical response upon resonant photoexcitation of the A exciton across a broad range of photoexcitation densities. In agreement with previously reported measurements we observe that the A exciton quenches gradually with increasing excitation density. However, a detailed lineshape analysis unveils an abrupt red shift in the transient peak positions of the A and B exciton resonances above an excitation density threshold. This is attributed to band gap renormalization arising from the formation of free charge carrier plasma, i.e., the EMT. The plasma phase decays with a time constant of 0.65 ps back into the excitonic state. The abrupt appearance of the plasma phase at the threshold density suggests that the EMT is a discontinuous and not a continuous transition. This work demonstrates how transient optical spectroscopy combined with lineshape analysis of two excitonic resonances simultaneously can be used to investigate the EMT in 2D materials.
papers.title: Discontinuous character of the ultrafast exciton Mott transition in monolayer WS$_2$

papers.abstract: We generalize the augmented Roothaan-Hall (ARH) Hessian formalism to the self-consistent field (SCF) optimization of spin-restricted open-shell (RO) wavefunctions, encompassing high-spin, low-spin, and two-determinant electronic states. A detailed ARH formulation is presented. We demonstrate that ARH is a highly efficient optimization algorithm for rapidly identifying accurate SCF solutions, primarily owing to its systematic construction of an effective Hessian, particularly in the case of Euclidean quadratic energy functions. The ARH is built upon a universal energy formulation, including grid-based integration, for spin-restricted closed-shell, spin-unrestricted and RO density functional theory (DFT), thereby unifying and simplifying their numerical implementation. The performance of the present method is evaluated using two benchmarking studies. First, for a series of iron-sulfur clusters exhibiting different spin states, which represent notoriously challenging SCF problems, the ARH algorithm demonstrates superior convergence efficiency relative to L-BFGS and truncated Newton methods, requiring much fewer RO-SCF iterations to achieve convergence. Second, the ARH approach tends to avoid convergence to higher-energy stationary points in two-determinant RO-SCF calculations for singlet excited states of selected photoactive compounds. Finally, an application of the ARH-based RO-SCF is illustrated by an investigation of the mechanistic origin of the spin-crossover phenomenon in Ni(II)-porphyrin complex utilized as a contrast agent.
papers.title: Augmented Roothaan-Hall Hessian Applied to Spin-Restricted Open-Shell Density-Functional Theory

papers.abstract: We propose a quantum algorithm that simulates the propagation of a light field through a weakly inhomogeneous medium. In the paraxial approximation, the wave equation in an inhomogeneous material takes the form of the Schrödinger equation with a time-dependent Hamiltonian. This reduction is used to simulate wave optical dynamics on a quantum computer. Beam propagator operators for a short propagation distance are constructed using an efficient and flexible block-encoding that enables the simulation of various optical setups. The algorithm is showcased by simulating the propagation of a one-dimensional Gaussian beam through a lens of finite thickness, and the resulting spherical aberration is demonstrated.
papers.title: Quantum simulation of wave optics in weakly inhomogeneous media using block-encoding

papers.abstract: Aircraft outer mould lines are often heavily constrained early by payload requirements, manufacturability limits, and low-observability considerations. The remaining aerodynamic design space is typically small, highly constrained, and difficult to represent using a concise and physically meaningful set of design variables. A structural modal parameterisation method (MPM) is introduced for such problems. The method constructs a tunable pseudo-structure and solves its eigenvalue problem to obtain a modal basis, from which a selected subset of modes parameterises the geometry. Boundary conditions, stiffness distribution, density, thickness, and added masses are treated as intentional basis-design variables that shape the admissible deformation space prior to optimisation. The resulting design coordinates are independent of any specific flow solver, making the approach broadly applicable. For tightly constrained aerodynamic shape optimisation problems, it provides a practical balance of parameter conciseness, robust constraint awareness, and geometric flexibility.
papers.title: Geometry Parameterisation via a Structural Modal Basis for Aerodynamic Shape Optimisation

papers.abstract: Context. Ultraluminous X-ray sources (ULXs) are thought to be powered, in many cases, by super-Eddington accretion onto compact objects. While soft X-ray lags have been detected in several ULXs, hard lags remain rare and poorly understood. Aims. We investigate the temporal and energy dependence of X-ray lags in NGC 7456 ULX-1 to constrain their physical origin and probe the super-Eddington accretion flow. Methods. We analyzed the two deepest XMM-Newton observations, taken in 2018 and 2023. Hard (1-10 keV) and soft (0.3-1 keV) light curves were cross-correlated using adaptive-binning techniques optimized for Poissonian low-count data. We measured lags over consecutive 10 ks intervals and investigated their energy dependence. Spectra were modeled using thermal and Comptonization models. Results. We detect significant hard X-ray lags in both observations, with the hard emission delayed by $\sim 10^3$ s during phases of rapid flux variability. The delays are primarily driven by the lowest-energy photons. Spectral modeling indicates a Comptonization-dominated flow comprising a cooler, extended outer region and a hotter, compact inner flow embedded in an optically thick wind. We interpret the delays as the combined effect of inward propagation of accretion-rate fluctuations and photon diffusion within the dense outflow. Fluctuations first enhance the soft-emitting outer regions and then propagate toward the hotter inner flow, where photons undergo stronger Comptonization before escaping with a kilosecond delay. The small inferred inner emitting radius disfavors an intermediate-mass black hole accretor. Conclusions. The sign, amplitude, and energy dependence of the delays disfavor standard reverberation. Propagation-driven variability coupled with radiative transfer in optically thick winds appears to play a major role in shaping the timing properties of super-Eddington accretion flows.
papers.title: Detection of kilosecond hard lags in the new pulsating ULX candidate NGC 7456 ULX-1
